steps.body: **Volume** counts the unit cubes that fill a box: a 2×3 base holds 6 cubes per layer, and 4 layers stack to 24 cubes — which is exactly **V = length × width × height** = 2×3×4 = 24 cubic units. The formula is layer-counting, compressed.

widget.prompt: A box has a 5×2 base and is 3 tall. How many unit cubes fill it?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 is ONE layer (5×2). Stack 3 of them: 10 × 3 = 30.
62 is the SURFACE AREA of this box, not its volume. Volume multiplies the three dimensions: 5×2×3 = 30.

widget.prompt: Find the volume of a 4×3×6 box.

commonErrors.feedback: 13 ADDS the dimensions (4+3+6). Volume MULTIPLIES them: 4×3×6 = 72.
108 is this box's SURFACE AREA — a different measurement. Volume is 4×3×6 = 72.

steps.body: Volume and surface area part ways here for good: volume is **cubic units** (what fits inside); surface area is **square units** (what covers outside). One box, two numbers: the 4×3×6 box holds 72 cubic units inside and wears 108 square units of surface. Keep the units straight and you'll never mix them.

explanationVariants: Filling is an INSIDE question — volume, measured in cubic units.

widget.prompt: "How much sand fills a sandbox?" — which measurement, and which units?

options.label: Volume, in cubic units
options.feedback: Right — filling the inside is volume, and volume always carries cubic units.

options.label: Surface area, in square units
options.feedback: Surface area covers the OUTSIDE. Sand fills the INSIDE — that's volume, in cubic units.

options.label: Volume, in square units
options.feedback: Right measurement, wrong units — volume is always CUBIC units, since it counts cubes.

predict.prompt: The 5-by-4 base holds 20 cubes in each layer. Before you build, what height should make exactly 60 cubes?
predict.reveal: The model reaches 60 cubes at height 3 because each layer adds 20 cubes: 20 + 20 + 20 = 60. Dividing by the whole base area, 60 ÷ 20, finds the number of layers.

widget.prompt: A box has volume 60, a length of 5, and a width of 4. What is its height? Set the height until the box holds 60 cubes.

commonBuilds.feedback: 12 divides by only the length (60 ÷ 5). Divide by the whole base area: 60 ÷ 20 = 3.

widget.lowFeedback: That box holds fewer than 60 cubes. The 5-by-4 base holds 20 per layer, so add layers.
widget.highFeedback: That box holds more than 60 cubes. Each layer adds 20, so 60 needs exactly three.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents volume formula.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for volume formula must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines volume formula.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Volume 2×2×5 = 20 cubic units; its surface area (2(4+10+10) = 48) is a different number answering a different question.
The same box carries both numbers — 20 inside, 48 outside.

widget.prompt: What is the VOLUME of a 2×2×5 box?

commonErrors.feedback: 48 is this box's SURFACE AREA. The question asks VOLUME: 2×2×5 = 20.

explanationVariants: 3×4×2 = 24 doubles to 3×4×4 = 48 — doubling ONE dimension doubles the volume.
Volume scales with each dimension: one doubling in, one doubling out.

widget.prompt: A 3×4×2 box has its height doubled (to 4). What is the NEW volume?

commonErrors.feedback: 26 adds 2 to the old volume (24+2). Doubling a dimension DOUBLES the whole volume: 3×4×4 = 48.
192 doubles ALL THREE dimensions (6×8×4). Only the height doubled: 3×4×4 = 48.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 3 × 4 × 4 = 48 — double one dimension, double the volume.

takeaways: V = length × width × height — the formula is stacked layer-counting.
Volume is cubic units (inside); surface area is square units (outside).
Doubling one dimension doubles the volume.
steps.teaser: next: what happens when an edge isn't a whole number.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Multiply all three dimensions.** A 2×3×4 box: base layer 2×3 = 6 cubes, stacked 4 high: 6 × 4 = 24 cubic units. Adding the dimensions (2+3+4 = 9) is the classic slip.

widget.prompt: Find the volume of a 2×3×4 box.

commonErrors.feedback: 52 is the SURFACE AREA of this box. Volume is 2×3×4 = 24.
